problem: summarize_crawl in scripts/dev_acceptance_stage.py kept only route and reason flags, so acceptance-crawl.json and the check:management-crawl detail dropped routes[].failedReads that execute-plans #1108 (FE-CRAWL-FAILED-READ-DETAIL-20261126, 9d540804) records; a failed route did not say which read failed.

solution.summary: Each failed route in summarize_crawl now carries failedReads (allowlisted copy) and failedReadsOmitted when the crawl manifest has them; ok routes and pre-#1108 manifests are summarized exactly as before. The failed check detail names the first counted failed read per route.
fields_kept: path (pathname only: scheme, host, query keys and values, fragment removed)
status (int) or error (first token of the error text, query removed, e.g. net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET; else the allowlisted reason; else request_failed)
reason (only one of the six upstream reason codes)
solution.fields_dropped: everything else in a read entry, including pending, honestNotFound, streamRule and any header, cookie, url or body field; the whole summary is still passed through the existing redact() with the minted token and environment

caps.order: counted reads first, then the rest in manifest order
caps.omitted: failedReadsOmitted = reads dropped by these caps + upstream failedReadsOmitted

solution.upstream_caps: execute-plans keeps 12 per route and 300 per run; this artifact is the release record, so the run cap is lower

new_tests: test_failed_reads_are_carried_bounded_per_route_and_run: 12 failed routes x 21 reads -> 12 per route, 100 per run, omitted counts, ok route carries nothing, detail names first counted read

test_failed_reads_strip_query_values_and_header_like_fields: query values, fragment, host, headers, cookie, body, url, free-text error tail and streamRule never reach check or artifact; bool status and string elapsed are not trusted
test_manifest_without_failed_reads_summarizes_as_before: the 45684275970 replay manifest (no failedReads) yields the same failedRoutes as before

acceptance_crawl_json_bytes_per_release.method: synthetic manifests through summarize_crawl, serialized as in crawl_check (routes, failedRoutes, nonGetRequests, counts)

runtime_budget.verdict_detail: unchanged bound: check detail is still clipped by DETAIL_LIMIT (2000 chars); failedRoutes on the check stays capped at MAX_FAILED_ROUTES (50)
runtime_budget.notes: no new process, request or file; the crawl runs once per release as before

hosted_proof: not run in this task: the next release whose crawl has a failed route will show failedReads in acceptance-crawl.json and the first failed read in check:management-crawl
residual_findings: Registered in docs/operations/problem-register.md: RC1 WP1.2 row for 503s under crawl load (persona-fleet, human-inbox readiness_blocker detail), keeping both sides: execute-plans #1108 evidence says load, the existing RC6 row says the human-inbox detail fans out across all five contributors.

Registered in docs/operations/problem-register.md: RC4 row for GET /bff/events/stream 409 replay_unavailable x35 in a 17-minute crawl (reconnect storm), keeping both sides: the crawl excuses the 409 as handled, the evidence calls the rate a defect.
The error name for a network failure is the first token of upstream free text; if a browser ever formats it differently the field falls back to the reason code, never to the full message.
